### Goal: Exploring the notion of chance and how it applies to significance measures, and understanding the role of the assumptions made by specific tests (e.g. the t-test) using simulations based on known distributions such as rnorm() and dbinom() and applying do real world data from DuckDB/Parquet respository.



### 1.Simulation based on rnorm, to study the performance of the “unbiased” estimator of standard deviation( n, n-1 & n-2 denominators)

```{r}

#### Setting up looping numbers ####
################################
max.sample.size <- 20
n.sim <- 10000 # number of re-samplings we are going to run for each sample size

#### Setting up matrices to save data. 

sd.n <- matrix(0, nrow = n.sim , ncol =  max.sample.size) # table of data for sd with n
sd.ori <- matrix(0, nrow = n.sim, ncol = max.sample.size) # table of data for sd with n-1
sd.n2 <- matrix(0, nrow = n.sim, ncol = max.sample.size) # table of data for sd with n-2

# sqrt(  sum((x - mean(x))^2) / (n-1)    )  

x_sd_n <-  function( data){
  n = length( data)
  sqrt(  sum((data - mean(data))^2) / n )
}

x_sd_n2 <- function( data){
    n = length( data)
  sqrt(  sum((data - mean(data))^2) / (n-2) )
}

#### perform computations in a loop ####
########################################
for (sample.size in 2:max.sample.size) {
   for (i.sim in 1:n.sim) { # resample n.sim times. In each iteration:
    samp <- rnorm( sample.size , mean = 0 , sd = 1) 
    
    # first set of sd ( n)
    sd.n [ i.sim , sample.size] <-  x_sd_n(samp)
    
    #second set of sd ( n-1)
    
    sd.ori [ i.sim , sample.size] <- sd(samp)
    
    # third set of sd ( n-2)
    
    sd.n2 [i.sim , sample.size] <- x_sd_n2(samp)
  
   }
}
```


### calculating the mean and spread of each of these three standard deviation estimates across all 𝑁 for current n


```{r}

n <- 2:max.sample.size 

#apply( X = "DATAFRAME" , MARGIN = "2 -columns /. "1 - rows" , )

#mean and spread for sd.n
sd.n_mean <- apply(X = sd.n [, n], MARGIN =  2, FUN = mean) 
sd.n_spread <- apply( sd.n[ , n] , 2, sd )

#mean and spread for sd.ori ( n-1)

sd.ori_mean <- apply(sd.ori[, n], 2, mean)
sd.ori_spread <- apply(sd.ori[, n], 2, sd )

#mean and spread for sd.n2 ( n-2)

sd.n2_mean <- apply(sd.n2[, n], 2, mean)
sd.n2_spread <- apply(sd.n2[, n], 2, sd )


#summary table
# 
# dfr <- data.frame( n = n,
#                    sd.n_mean =sd.n_mean,
#                    sd.ori_mean = sd.ori_mean,
#                    sd.n2_mean = sd.n2_mean,
#                    
#                    sd.n_spread = sd.n_spread,
#                    sd.ori_spread = sd.ori_spread,
#                    sd.n2_spread = sd.n2_spread)

```


### Plot the calculated means and spreads of all three estimators of the standard deviation as functions of sample size 𝑛

```{r}

# spreads across the 3 estimators of sd. against n 

plot( n, sd.n2_spread, type ="n", ylim = c(0, 1) , main = "
      spreads across  3 estimators(n, n-1, n-2) of sd. for n =20 ",
      xlab = "sample size",
      ylab = "standard deviation estimates") 

points( n , sd.n_spread , pch = 19 , col= "green" )
points( n , sd.ori_spread , pch = 15, col = "red")
points( n , sd.n2_spread , pch = 4 , col ="blue")


#means across the 3 estimators of mean against n

plot( n, sd.n2_spread, type ="n" , ylim = c(0, 2) ,  main = "
      means across  3 estimators(n, n-1, n-2) of sd. for n =20 ",
      xlab = "sample size",
      ylab = "mean sd estimates") 

points( n , sd.n_mean , pch = 19 , col= "green" ) # n
points( n , sd.ori_mean , pch = 10, col = "red") # n-1
points( n , sd.n2_mean, pch = 4 , col ="black") #n-2






```


### 2: Behavior of the t-test under the null hypothesis using numerical simulation.


```{r}

arb_mean <- 2
arb_var <- 3 ; arb_sd = sqrt(arb_var)
n1 <- 7
n2 <- 9
smpl_1 <- rnorm( n1, mean = arb_mean , sd = sqrt( arb_var))
smpl_2 <- rnorm( n2, mean = arb_mean , sd = sqrt(arb_var))

#Ho: mean of smpl_1 - smpl_2 = 0
#Ha:mean of smpl_1 - smpl_2 != 0

#mean difference of smpl_1 and smpl_2

mean.diff_smpl1_2 <- mean(smpl_1) - mean( smpl_2)

t.test( smpl_1 , smpl_2 , var.equal = TRUE) # since both sample were generated from 
#via rnorm with both mean and sd known.

# 	Two Sample t-test
# 
# data:  smpl_1 and smpl_2
# t = 1.7874, df = 14, p-value = 0.09554
# alternative hypothesis: true difference in means is not equal to 0
# 95 percent confidence interval:
#  -0.2823871  3.1066603
# sample estimates:
# mean of x mean of y 
#  2.754624  1.342488 

p_value = t.test( smpl_1 , smpl_2 , var.equal = TRUE)$p.value
p_value

#evidence is consistent with the Ho. hypothesis as p.value (0.09553928) > 0.05

```

### resmapling functions

```{r}

rsmpl <- function( n1, n2, n.sim = 10000, mu = 2, sd = sqrt(3) ) {
  
  #### Step 1: create a matrix containing the resamplings (10,000 rows for the simulations and 12 columns for the resamplings).
  ## Step 1: the resampling matrix — n.sim rows x (n1 + n2) columns.
  simulation_matrix <- matrix( rnorm(n.sim * (n1 + n2), mean = mu, sd = sd), nrow = n.sim, ncol = n1 + n2) 


 #### Step 2: define a function that will calculate the difference between the means of sample 1 and sample 2 in our representation of the data such as:
 mean.diff <- function(x) mean(x[1:n1])-mean(x[(n1+1):(n1+n2)])

# Step 3: calculate the difference in the means for all rows of your matrix. Save it in an object called #sim.diff.

sim.diff <- apply(simulation_matrix, 1, mean.diff)

t.test_p_values <- apply(simulation_matrix, 1, function(x) t.test(x[1:n1], x[(n1 + 1):(n1 + n2)])$p.value)


#### Step 4: calculate the brute force p-value by taking the rank of the negative absolute value of sim.diff divided by the length of sim.diff. Save this in a vector called sim.p.rk

sim.p.rk <- rank( -abs(sim.diff) ) / length(sim.diff)

list( n1 =n1 , n2 =n2 , sim.diff = sim.diff , sim.p.rk = sim.p.rk , t.test_p_values = t.test_p_values)
}


```


### visual analysis- plots

- the distribution of differences observed in all the resamplings
- the distribution of t-test p-values obtained for the pairs of samples in each resampling
- the distribution of brute-force p-values obtained for the pairs of samples in each resampling
- a scatter plot of t-test p-values versus the differences between the means in each pair of samples drawn
- a scatter plot of brute-force p-values versus the differences between the means (in this scatterplot, each point should represent a single resampling experiment, x-axis = difference, y-axis = p-value)
- a scatter plot of t-test p-values vs brute-force p-values

```{r}

 # (b) distribution of t-test p-values

    # (e) brute-force p vs mean difference

    # (f) t.test_p-values vs brute-force p-values
    plot( mtrix$t.test_p_values, mtrix$sim.p.rk , pch = 20, cex = 0.1, col = rainbow(2),
          cex.main =.9,
         main = "t-test p-values VS brute-force p-values", xlab = "brute-force p", 
         ylab = "t-test p")

}
```
